sections.heading: Define the rooms and the existing condition
sections.text: Send the villa location, rooms or areas being changed, current photographs and any available drawings. Separate a kitchen or wardrobe upgrade from a wider renovation. Identify items to retain, remove or replace, and record anything that needs a site check before the scope is agreed.

sections.heading: Plan access around the household
sections.text: Say whether the property will be occupied during the work. Agree access, delivery routes, protection of retained finishes and how work areas will be separated. Review any phased handover or restricted working periods for this property rather than assuming the whole villa is available throughout.

sections.heading: Release kitchens and wardrobes against details
sections.text: Joinery needs agreed dimensions, materials, finishes and internal arrangements before production. Share appliance information and storage requirements, and identify items supplied by others. Record samples and drawing revisions so a later change can be reviewed for its effect on scope, cost and timing.

sections.heading: Assign services and approval responsibilities
sections.text: Bathroom, kitchen and lighting changes need clear interfaces with the relevant services. Identify who checks the existing condition, prepares drawings and handles any required community, developer or authority submissions. Record responsibilities and exclusions in the proposal rather than assuming a universal approval package.

sections.heading: Agree checks before handover
sections.text: Separate design decisions, production, site work and final checks in the programme. Set out the agreed finishes, responsibility for service testing, outstanding items and handover information. Review unresolved approvals, materials and supplier interfaces before treating a desired move-in or handover date as confirmed.

sections.heading: Choose a contractor against the actual Abu Dhabi brief
sections.text: Give each stand contractor the same show name, venue, hall, stand number, dimensions and open sides. Explain the products, demonstrations, reception, meetings and storage you need. Ask for a proposal that identifies the work and responsibilities, so an exclusion is not mistaken for a lower price.

sections.heading: What to agree for an ADNEC exhibition stand
sections.text: Use the current organiser manual and venue information for this show. Record who prepares drawings, submits them, responds to comments and orders utilities or overhead services. Confirm the access, installation and dismantling windows. The agreed scope, not a general contractor label, determines who does each task. No venue approval outcome is guaranteed.

sections.heading: Separate design deliverables from construction documents
sections.text: Agree the layout and concept visuals needed to review the stand, then identify the drawings, material details and specialist inputs needed for the proposed build. A rendered image helps explain the appearance; it does not replace structural calculations, service drawings or a required venue submission.

sections.heading: Fabrication supported by our Umm Al Quwain workshop
sections.text: The FANN joinery workshop supports production of the agreed stand elements. Confirm drawing revisions, quantities, materials and finish details before release. Identify specialist suppliers and service interfaces separately. Workshop photographs do not establish every trade, material grade, structural capacity or engineering approval.

sections.heading: Identify transport, installation and dismantling
sections.text: Name the parties responsible for transport, venue access, installation, handover checks, on-site support and dismantling. Mark storage, reuse and transport after the show as included, excluded or supplied by others. The programme must reflect the current show schedule and the agreed work, not a standard build duration.

sections.heading: Compare stand builders on the same included work
sections.text: Check the quoted structure, joinery, finishes, graphics, furniture, AV and lighting against the same brief. Confirm utilities, rigging, organiser charges, approvals and later changes separately. Share any existing stand elements intended for reuse so their condition and suitability can be reviewed before the proposal is agreed.

sections.heading: Choose modular for a repeatable show programme
sections.text: A modular approach uses a configurable system that may support several events. Compare the available components against each allocation, open side, product display and graphic format. Reuse works when the next layout still meets the brief.

sections.heading: Choose custom for a specific experience
sections.text: A custom build offers freedom over structure, finishes and visitor activities for a particular brief. It can suit an unusual allocation or a distinctive product experience. Reuse of any custom elements must be planned, not assumed.

sections.heading: Compare the complete logistics
sections.text: Ask about packing, transport, installation crew, storage, maintenance and replacement graphics between shows. Neither approach has a universal price or installation duration: compare the same scope and event programme.

sections.heading: Questions to ask before deciding
sections.text: Which parts are reused? What changes for the next show? Who stores and inspects the elements? What is the cost of reconfiguration and new graphics? Ask for the proposal to distinguish fabrication, logistics and event services.

faqs.question: What is the best option for our stand?
faqs.answer: Start with your allocation, products, visitor activities, show schedule and budget. Compare proposals against the same requirements rather than a generic recommendation.

faqs.question: Can we compare both options before choosing?
faqs.answer: Yes. Send the brief and ask for the proposed design, scope and responsibilities to be made clear so you can compare like for like.

faqs.question: Is one option always cheaper?
faqs.answer: No universal price applies. Materials, dimensions, graphics, services, transport, storage and installation affect the total for the actual job.

faqs.question: What should we send for a quote?

faqs.answer: Confirm the submission responsibilities and any specialist reviews or services in the proposal for your show and design.

faqs.answer: Share your brief using the stand quote form. FANN can then discuss the scope and next design step.

sections.text: An agency may coordinate strategy, creative work and a network of fabricators and specialist suppliers. Outsourcing alone does not establish poor quality. Ask who builds each element, who supervises it and who is accountable for delivery.
